legibility: 1533: McGill (600 ppi, colour) is the sharpest and is the recommended tracing source; LOC (IIIF, ~3200-3600 px page width, crops fetched losslessly as PNG regions) is equally clean; Jung/e-rara (2550 px pages) is smaller but legible, and is a different setting of the II.22 tables. Every crop was viewed. The checker found four crops that cut something off (1651 Saturn Wellcome and EEB seal ring-ends, 1651 Mercury seal foot, 1651 colligantia labels) and re-cut them from the same raw pages; nothing is now cut off. In the 1533 Hebrew fount daleth and resh are hard to tell apart (daleth has a squared top-right corner, resh a rounded one), and he/heth differ only by a hair-gap at the top of the left leg; readings rely on context and side-by-side comparison. 1651 Wellcome (360 ppi) is legible but shows strong show-through; on p. 246 the Sun table column 1 and the left of the seal are hidden at the outer (left) edge of the verso - the EEB microfilm crop of p. 246 is complete. EEB microfilm is bitonal-looking greyscale with manuscript corrections in the squares.
problems: Chamber 8 in all three 1533 copies prints ח פ ת: the third letter is the same tav sort used in chamber 4, not final pe ף (the class list on p. CCLXXIIII does print ף). The 1651 cut prints a final pe.
1651 grid: chamber 7 has only two letters (a zayin-like form and ayin; no final nun); chamber 1's middle letter is a nun-like curve rather than yod.
1651 prints the single Michael character upside down relative to 1533.
Moon square: row 1 col 8 is 45 (not 54) in all three 1533 copies, in both the abaco and the Hebrew table, and in the 1651 Wellcome copy.

1651 Wellcome copy (uncorrected print): Mercury rows 3, 4 and 6 contain duplicates (45 x3, 38 x2, 25 x2) and lack 48, 35, 28, 46; Venus row 6 col 2 = 38 (1533: 39); Moon 78 and 75 are exchanged (row 1 col 2 = 75, row 7 col 8 = 78). The EEB microfilm copy shows pen corrections at these cells, which probably explains the EEBO-TCP readings the research used.
Jupiter Hebrew 15: טו in McGill and Jung, יה in LOC.
Bne Seraphim is numbered 1225 in the LOC copy, 1252 in McGill, Jung and 1651.

CCLXXVI. 1651: pp. 441-444 (grid and figures p. 442, Michael p. 443, ligatures p. 444).

Grid layout CONFIRMED: Hebrew order row by row from the top right (chamber 1 = top right ... chamber 9 = bottom left), letters within each cell right to left; the research's assumed layout and its nine figures are right. The nine figures are printed left to right in chamber order 1-9 with no labels and no points.

Points as printed (1533): short slanted ticks above each figure, to its upper left; counts in the five-figure Michael: מ 2, י 2, כ 2, א 1, ל 2 (left to right on the page: ל א כ י מ). In the three-figure row the contracted pairs keep their points (2+1, 2+2, 2). The single character has none, as the text says. These counts hold for McGill and LOC. The Jung copy prints ONE point over kaph in the five-figure row (so 2, 1, 1, 2, 2 left to right) and one point over the kaph upright of the second contracted figure (1+2).

II.22 locators (1533): heading at foot of p. CXLV; text pp. CXLV-CXLVIII; names table p. CXLVIII and top of CXLIX; Saturn and Jupiter p. CXLIX (sig. n3r); Mars and Sun p. CL; Venus p. CLI (sig. n4r); Mercury p. CLII; Moon p. CLIII; ch. 23 begins p. CLIIII. 1651: pp. 239-252 as in the research.

1533 prints every square twice, 'in abaco' (Arabic numerals) and 'in notis Hebraicis'; the Hebrew cells stand in the same left-to-right positions as the numbers. 15 and 16 are written יה and יו (Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon in every copy checked), except Jupiter's 15 noted above.

Seven 1533 squares agree with the research's squares except the Moon's 45 for 54 (all copies). Mercury 1533 is the research's magic square exactly. The Hebrew-letter tables carry their own slips: the Sun's 33 is printed גל (transposed) in all three copies; the Mars 23 is printed גכ (transposed) in the Jung copy only; the LOC copy leaves the Mercury cell for 10 (row 2 col 7) blank.
Mars' fifth name (25) is printed in Hebrew only, יהי, already in 1533 (no Latin), answering the research's open question about the 1651 entry.

Moon: 1533 prints the seal, one figure 'Dæmonij Lunæ', two figures under 'Dæmonij dæmoniorum Lunæ' and two under 'Intelligentiæ Intelligentiarum Lunæ'; there is no single-intelligence character for the Moon.

The three 1533 copies are not one setting: LOC and McGill have large ruled tables but differ in details (stops after numbers, 1225/1252, Jupiter 15); the Jung copy sets all II.22 tables compactly with underscored cells and moves the figures to the right-hand column. The seal woodcuts look alike in all three; they were not compared stroke by stroke.
1651 seals were not compared figure by figure except the Sun (ring-ends at three corners, not four).
